usages.explain: Used to point out, as an example, a specific content expressed by the noun following it. The noun following indicates a higher-level concept than the one expressed by the preceding noun.

examples.content: 妹は、キムパプのような簡単な料理しか作れません。
examples.transcription: いもうとは、きむぱぷのようなかんたんなりょうりしかつくれません。
examples.mean: My sister can only make simple dishes like kimbap.

examples.content: 「アポ」のような外来語は、とても難しいですね。
examples.transcription: 「あぽ」のようながいらいごは、とてもむずかしいですね。
examples.mean: Foreign words like "apo" are very difficult to understand.

usages.explain:
Note: In the case of receiving a noun phrase, even without "ような", a sentence can be formed, but whether or not "ような" is included, the meaning of the sentence will be different.
Example: In the case of "処方薬を飲んでもよくならないような場合"
It means there are many other cases besides this one, and we're just using this case as an example.
If "ような" is omitted, this is a statement limited to a specific case.

title: のような... => just like; just as; similar to..
